messages.author: 2060c8e54fb73471
messages.subject: Pairwise estimation procedure with mirt
parts:
Hello, 

I am trying to replicate a partial credit model analysis.
In the original paper "The pairwise estimation procedure implemented in the soft-
ware program RUMM2030 was used to estimate item parameters in the partial credit Rasch model for dichotomous and polytomous items [26]."

This is the work which I am trying to replicate: https://www.valueinhealthjournal.com/article/S1098-3015(13)01867-6/fulltext?_returnURL=https%3A%2F%2Flinkinghub.elsevier.com%2Fretrieve%2Fpii%2FS1098301513018676%3Fshowall%3Dtrue

And this is the one the authors refer to (ref #26): Andrich D, Luo G. Conditional pairwise estimation in the Rasch model for ordered response categories using principal components. J Appl Meas 2003;4:205–21.

 I'm quite new at IRT analysis, (I have not been able to access Andrich's work in full yet) and I am not quite sure:
- how does pairwise estimation differ from other estimation methods?
- is it possible to achieve it with mirt? And if yes, how?

I'd be grateful to anyone who can help me out or at least point me in the right direction

Federica Conte

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Pairwise estimation procedure with mirt
parts:
mirt doesn't currently support this pairwise estimation algorithm; it is restricted to marginal ML/Baysian estimation only. Regarding your questions, from what I can tell the algorithm is just using different count tables to compute the parameters, which has it's advantages/disadvantages like all other approaches (could be impeller to implement than CML estimation, for instance, and may avoid the use of a prior ability distribution which is required for MML estimation). Is there some reason you prefer using this algorithm verses CML (available in the eRm package) and MML (available in mirt)?

Phil

messages.subject: Re: Pairwise estimation procedure with mirt
parts:
dear Phil,
Thank  you for your answer.
I do not have a theoretical reason for choosing one algorithm over another, at the moment. I want to validate a questionnaire on an Italian sample, and since it is my first time analyzing polytomous items, I started off following the analysis from the original paper as closely as possible. I used mirt because it's what I used to run IRT in the past (for a 2PL model of dichotomous items). 

Sorry to bother you more, but is there any reference you would suggest about how to test a PCM? I am struggling to build up the "background knowledge" necessary to make informed and correct choices in this analysis

Federica Conte
